A brand identity and strategy project reimagining how AI companies present themselves online — embracing searchability and human-centred, blog-based content organization instead of conversion-focused web design trends. The identity itself was conceived as "a maze with no entrance nor exit," reflecting the exploratory nature of AI development.

title: UKAI Projects
credits: Brand Strategy, Creative Direction, and Design by Luisa Ji and Nour Bishouty
description:
[NOTE: the brand/identity work described here doesn't appear as a dated line item in Luisa's latest CV paste, though her role as Director of UKAI Projects is confirmed there — confirm this case study should still stand on its own before publishing.]

Brand strategy and creative direction for UKAI Projects, a Toronto-based cultural organization founded by Jerrold McGrath supporting artists and cultural entrepreneurs in volatile environments. Rather than a single logo, Luisa and Nour Bishouty developed multiple visual identities embracing chaos within constraints — "chaos within constraints, shapes shaped by constraints, and a collection of imperfect weirdness that delightfully surprises." The name draws on 鵜飼 (cormorant fishing), a Japanese practice symbolizing mutual care and fair exchange, in contrast to industrial efficiency models.
